Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

most adverb

to the greatest degree: most beautiful, like most

also the most, -est (biggest, fastest), as … as possible, above all

classical

Gell. 1.9.5: rērum omnium difficillimās
Lewis & Short s.v. superlātīvus: nōmen, in the superlative degree (Charisius, Priscian)

gradus superlātīvus

the superlative degree of an adjective or adverb (cārissimus, difficillimus), with a genitive or ex for the group

the superlative: hardest, most beautiful

Latin says “most” with the ending: difficillimus, the hardest; the group is in the genitive: rērum omnium difficillimās. The superlative also means “very”. With quam, “as … as possible”: quam plūrima, as much as possible (Quint. 11.2.41).

Other words

  • maximē — most, especially, above all

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.5: suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur; Plin. NH 8.29: animālium maximē ōdēre mūrem

    With verbs, and with adjectives that make no superlative; also “above all”: maximē autem date operam ut valeātis (Cic. Fam. 14.18.2).

  • plūrimum — most, very much (with verbs: be able, be worth)

    adverb · also used · classical · Ps.-Publil. I 15: In sterculīnō plūrimum gallus potest.

    Plūrimum posse, to have the most power (see a lot).

Examples

  • ubi rēs didicerant rērum omnium difficillimās, tacēre audīreque

    when they had learned the hardest things of all, to keep quiet and to listenGell. 1.9.5

  • suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur

    for each of us is led most by his own interestsCic. Fin. 5.5

  • animālium maximē ōdēre mūrem

    of all animals they hate the mouse mostPlin. NH 8.29

  • Semper cōnsilium tunc deest, cum opus est maximē.

    Good advice is always missing just when it is needed most.Publil. Sent. S 31

  • In sterculīnō plūrimum gallus potest.

    On his own dunghill the cock is most powerful.Ps.-Publil. I 15

  • quārē et puerī statim, ut praecēpī, quam plūrima ēdiscant

    so let children, as I advised, learn by heart as much as possible from the startQuint. 11.2.41

See also most, more, least, a lot.

SourcesLewis & Short: superlativus · Lewis & Short: magnus (maximē) · Lewis & Short: plurimus

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius, loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-plinius, loci-publilius, loci-quintilianus, loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.

Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text; from N onwards that numbering differs from Meyer’s. “Ps.-Publil.” marks lines from the later collections printed with him.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
